speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your appointment. I see you're experiencing a pruritic rash on your trunk and extremities along with fever, runny nose, and headache. To better understand what is going on, have you had any recent close contact with individuals who have had similar symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Measles (Rubeola)

I have noted the classic progression of symptoms including the "3 Cs" (cough, coryza, conjunctivitis - though only coryza and headache were mentioned initially), the high fever, and specifically the maculopapular rash that started on the face and spread downward, sparing the perioral area. While this clinical picture is highly suggestive, I would like to confirm with a rapid diagnostic test. REQUEST TEST: Measles_IgM
